text.p: U.S.-Japan business leaders in the non-manufacturing sector see 115 yen to the dollar as a "comfortable level" for exchange rates, Fuji Bank chairman Toru Hashimoto said on Thursday.

Hashimoto co-chaired a group of service-sector executives from the United States and Japan that concluded a two-day meeting in San Francisco on Wednesday as part of a larger bilateral business meeting.

"Somebody suggested that probably 115 to the dollar is a very comfortable level and there was no particular disagreement," Hashimoto told Reuters Financial Television in an interview from San Francisco monitored here.
"As far as the services small group is concerned, it's more or less the consensus," he said.
More than 70 U.S. and Japanese business leaders issued a joint statement at the conclusion of the San Francisco meeting calling for stable exchange rates that reflect economic fundamentals.

"Efforts to improve economic fundamentals must continue so as to minimise the incipient rise in the Japanese trade-current account surplus, and thus to stabilise the yen-dollar exchange rate within an appropriate range reflecting basic fundamentals," the joint statement said.
Hashimoto said the service-sector executives agreed that "a stable exchange rate is good for all businesses".
But he said there was some difference of opinion within the San Francisco group about the longer-term trend in the dollar/yen rate.
Some Japanese executives in the joint group argued that higher Japanese productivity and lower inflation in Japan point to a gradual strengthening in the yen, he said.
But some U.S. executives countered that productivity is underestimated in the U.S. economy, he said.
